title: Unit Event — Deeper and Deeper

meta.Outline: Wonderlands×Showtime agrees to participate in a workshop run by ArcLand. As Rui takes the directors' course, he is confronted with something he's never realized about himself before.

rows.Speaker: Announcement
rows.Line:
<Welcome to Tokyo ArcLand.
The place where your most wonderful dreams come true.>

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Whoa...!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line:
Wow!
The ground's all sparkly and lit up!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: They're using interactive projection mapping.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Sensors detect guests' movements, and project interactive images to follow them.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line:
Hey, you're right.
The lights change colors as you walk.

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: This is so cool! And if you go hop-hoppity-hopscotch, then you can get them to pop and shimmer!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Wait, where are you going?!
We aren't here to enjoy the park, you know!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line:
*Gasp*
I forgot!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Honestly...

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Still, we've been to a lot of amazing places until now... But I really wasn't expecting to get a chance to train here.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Me neither. After all, ArcLand is one of the few world-class amusement parks that are able to compete against Riley Dream Park.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Naturally, its doors are not opened for very many at all...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: We really must thank Keisuke and Shosuke again.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: We get to train with a fourth troupe?!

rows.Speaker: Keisuke
rows.Line:
Yes, at ArcLand.
I'm sure you're all familiar.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: What...?!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: ArcLand? Where Asahi and his friends work?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Yes...
But ArcLand puts on some of the best shows in the world.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Why are we getting a chance to train there?
We have performed with them in the past, but even so...

rows.Speaker: Shosuke
rows.Line: We've actually been reaching out for quite a while now. Unlike last time, which both parties saw as a collaborative effort, this time we're asking them for a massive favor.

rows.Speaker: Shosuke
rows.Line: They kept turning us away, but we managed to get their approval just recently.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
I see.
But why now?

rows.Speaker: Keisuke
rows.Line: As you all know, ArcLand is home to many talented young actors and directors.

rows.Speaker: Keisuke
rows.Line: They're going to be holding an internal workshop as a way to help them improve their skills.

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: A workshop...?!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Could it be that... We've been invited to participate, as well?

rows.Speaker: Keisuke
rows.Line:
That's right.
They said that you'd be welcome to join if you're free.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: But an internal workshop will naturally be designed for the cast members and directors of ArcLand...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I have to think they're going to be running some very demanding activities.

rows.Speaker: Shosuke
rows.Line:
Yes, I agree.
But it should be a good experience for all of you.

rows.Speaker: Keisuke
rows.Line: What do you say? The decision is yours.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Of course we're going!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (After turning down their offer last time, I didn't think we'd be asked to work with them again.)

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: What's wrong, Nene? You keep looking all around.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Oh, so...

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: They said that someone would come and get us, so I was keeping an eye out for...
Hey!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Ah, right on cue!
se_run_men_001_1
Thank you all for waiting! Long time no see.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: And welcome to Tokyo ArcLand!

rows.Speaker: Emu & Nene
rows.Line: Asahi...?!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: You were sent to come and get us, Asahi?

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Yes! I volunteered when I heard that WXS would be coming to visit us!

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
The others also wanted to come...
But a big group would've been too conspicuous.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Oh, but don't worry! We decided by playing rock paper scissors, so it was all fair.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: R-Rock paper scissors...

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line:
You haven't changed at all, Asahi.
Even though all the shows, movies and TV dramas must be keeping you really busy.

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: Yeah! You're still as smiley and cheerful as ever!

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Today, we'll be having an orientation session regarding the workshop. So, let's head right over to where all the others are.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Excellent! Please lead the way!
se_walk_men_001_4

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line:
Fun, fun workshop♪
I wonder what we're gonna do☆

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Haha. You all sound very excited.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes, that's because we are!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Will you also be participating in this workshop, Asahi?

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Yes, I'll be there for what I can when I don't have any work engagements.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: It's just been so long since we last got to work with WXS. And besides, this workshop is probably going to be our best one yet.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: What do you mean?

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: It's going to be led by ArcLand's most veteran actors and directors.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Not only that, we've also invited some special guests.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Special guests?

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
Yes.
I'm sure you're also going to be surprised, Rui.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Me? Also...?)
se_walk_men_001_4

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Anyway, this is where it's taking place.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
First, you all need to say hi to everyone.
Some will be meeting Wonderlands×Showtime for the very first time.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: Hey, you guys!
Orientation Venue

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: I think it's safe to say that never before has ArcLand put on such a grand workshop.

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Workshop courses will take place in the gaps between normally scheduled practices and work, so it will likely be a very intensive experience.

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line:
But it should very much be worth it.
And we promise to provide you with all the support we can.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Asahi was right. They seem to be pulling out all the stops for this one.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (They have separate courses for actors and directors.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Plus, there will be a collaborative group assignment. I imagine the directors will devise shows, and the actors will perform them.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Hehe. I'm getting excited just thinking about it.)

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Now, I'd like to introduce the special instructors we've invited to join us for this workshop. First, for the actors' course...

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: We have Natalia Santi, Glen Barkin and Elio Sakurai.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: What...?!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Natalia Santi?
She's won several international awards for her performances in musical films.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I had heard that she's been helping young actors hone their skills lately... But I wasn't expecting to hear her name here.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line:
Me neither...
And Glen Barkin's one of the most famous actors on Broadway right now.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: He doesn't usually play the lead, but he has an incredible talent for playing memorable, demanding roles. His acting skills are supposed to be peerless...

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: Wow, that means they're all really amazing!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes, and Elio Sakurai is a world-class dancer.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: If I recall, he runs his own dance studio specifically tailored for performing in musicals.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Why do you know so much about him, Tsukasa?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: When we were taking ballet lessons at Morinomiya, I looked up videos on the subject. That was when I came across one of his explainer videos.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: And he doesn't just cover ballet. He has videos covering everything from jazz to theatre dance. I ended up binge-watching them because they were so fascinating.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes. They've gathered the best of the best.

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: I can't wait to talk to them!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But you need more than just deep pockets to get guests like these to teach at your workshop.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It's proof that ArcLand is just that invested in their shows, as well as the cast members who perform in them.)

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Next, I'd like to introduce the special guests we've invited for the directors' course.

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: Oh, Rui, it's time for the people who are gonna teach you!

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: After the names we just heard, my heart is kind of racing...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Mine too.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Getting to train here is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (We have to make the absolute most of it.)
Orientation Venue

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: We've invited two guests for the directors' course. One of them happens to be in attendance right now.

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Would you be kind enough to introduce yourself, Mr. Sakaki?

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Of course.

rows.Speaker: ArcLand Cast Member A
rows.Line:
Wait...
Sakaki? As in...?

rows.Speaker: ArcLand Director
rows.Line: Y-Yeah...
se_event_deeper_2025_001

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
Hello.
I believe I'm meeting most of you for the very first time.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
My name is Koryu Sakaki.
I'll be one of your teachers during this workshop.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Koryu Sakaki...?!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line:
I've seen him on TV before!
He's a really famous director, right?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, he is.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Koryu Sakaki... Becoming the youngest-ever recipient of the Jiro Kikukawa Award for Theatrical Performances made him a household name.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: He's renowned for his artistry, but he's also known throughout the entertainment industry for his movies and TV dramas...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes, whenever something becomes the talk of the town, you can bet you'll find his name in the credits.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: And he isn't just popular in Japan. He's famous all over the world. Some of the most storied theatres have asked him to produce shows for them.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: I remember reading a magazine article that called him “the busiest director in Japan”...

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: Wow. What kind of person do you think he is?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Well, based on his list of works, he seems like the artistic type with very particular preferences...

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: I'm really in no position to be teaching anyone anything...

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: But ArcLand has been so good to me, after all. I couldn't simply turn them down.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: In any case, if you find anything I say to be interesting, then I hope you're able to make use of it.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: So, let's all do our best together.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: He's much more modest than I was expecting.

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Yeah, I'm a bit surprised...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Yes, he seems like an interesting fellow...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Each of Koryu Sakaki's shows is unique in its own way.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It can be the most absurd, impenetrable piece of theatre or a show that's all laughs... Everything that he makes possesses its own “flavor”.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (He has an uncanny ability to bring a character's innermost thoughts, good and bad, to the surface, and present them in a fiercely captivating manner.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: They definitely outdid themselves by bringing him here...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(...?
That expression he just made...)

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Rui? Is something wrong?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Oh, no. It's nothing.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (He reminded me of someone else for a second there...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But I might've just been imagining things.)

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Thank you very much, Mr. Sakaki.

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: Our second guest will be joining us remotely from abroad due to some scheduling issues.

rows.Speaker: Workshop Host
rows.Line: He's...
bgm_area00004
Wonderland SEKAI

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line: Wow, it sounds like this workshop is going to be incredible!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Yes!
Today was merely the orientation...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: But the venues they've provided and the guests they've invited as teachers are top-class!

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: I still can't believe it. This workshop is like a hundred times grander than I was expecting...

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: You've looked dazed ever since they finished explaining everything to us, Nene.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Oh, are you feeling alright?

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: I'm fine. I was just a bit overwhelmed...

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: But this is also an unbelievably valuable opportunity to learn from world-class professionals.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Right.
We're sure to grow a tremendous amount, as long as we don't shy away from this challenge.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Let's give it everything we've got!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: Yeah!!

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line: Hehe. You're so motivated!

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line:
Is something wrong, Rui?
Are you feeling sleepy?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Huh?

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: You've looked a little out of it for a while now.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: No, nothing's wrong.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: It's just... Somehow it hasn't entirely sunk in for me, I suppose.

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line: What hasn't sunk in?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: ArcLand invited two guests to come and teach us during this workshop.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: The first is Koryu Sakaki, one of Japan's most renowned directors. The second is...

rows.Speaker: Director
rows.Line: <It doesn't matter if you're rich or poor, clever or foolish, among the majority or minority...>

rows.Speaker: Director
rows.Line: <All people laugh, cry and feel anger in the same way...>

rows.Speaker: Director
rows.Line: <That is what ties us all together after bearing witness to a truly marvelous spectacle.>

rows.Speaker: Director
rows.Line: <My goal is to keep making shows that do just that.>

rows.Speaker: Director
rows.Line: <I believe that is the key to humanity becoming one... I believe that there's something unimaginably special awaiting us at the end of that path!>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Tom Gray.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: A director I admire very much.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: So Rui, you get to be taught by your hero?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Yes, so it seems.
Perhaps that's why nothing has felt quite real all afternoon.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I understand exactly how you feel!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I thought I was dreaming when I heard that Mr. Amami had come to see our show!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Hehe. I remember.
It's difficult to believe that these things could actually happen.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: If I could somehow tell my younger self this would happen, I'm sure he wouldn't believe me.

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line:
I see...
This Mr. Gray really means a lot to you, doesn't he?

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Hehe. I wish I could tell little Rui the good news.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Did you know? In the future, you'll work very, very hard...

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: And someday, you'll get to meet your hero! That's what I would say.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Opportunity has come knocking, Rui!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I understand what you're feeling, but you need to focus and make this most of this golden opportunity!

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: You've got this, Rui!

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Zzz... Zzz...

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Rui... I believe in you...♪

rows.Speaker: MEIKO
rows.Line: That was pretty clear, for sleep talk.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Hehe...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Thank you all very much.
I plan on learning as much as I possibly can.
A few days later
ArcLand - Workshop Venue

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: And now, without further ado, I hereby declare the directors' course open.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: I'm not one for formalities, so I'll be keeping things casual from here on out.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: And I think it's high time we introduced our other teacher.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Hello. Can you all hear me?”>

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
“Yes, we can hear you.
We can also see your bedhead, Tom.”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Excellent. That means we're all set to begin.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It's not surprising that two world-class directors such as them would be on speaking terms...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But they seem like old friends.)

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
Ah, I almost forgot.
We'll be constantly switching back and forth between English and Japanese during this workshop.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: I'll be sure to translate any especially technical terms or phrases, but this is also training for when you go overseas for work in the future. So, try to keep up.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Please feel free to use the translation functions on your smartphones and computers. Tom will be doing just that.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“Hello, everyone.
I won't be able to be there in person due to work scheduling, but I've been looking forward to this workshop for a very long time.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I may be a teacher for this workshop, but I'm sure you all have much to teach me too.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“So, let's make the most of our time together.”>

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: We'll start by going over the workshop's goals.

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: The objective of the directors' course is to have you all produce shows from scratch.

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: We'll have you approach this assignment as though you're developing a show to be performed on stage at ArcLand.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: In other words, this show will need to meet the park's world-class standards...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Not only will it have to appeal to a wide range of age groups, it will need a high degree of artistic mastery.

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: We wish to see original ideas from all of you, so please refrain from deriving or adapting anything from existing works. Keeping it on the level of homage is fine.

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: And as far as casts go, you'll need to ask the actors in the other workshop course.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I see. In my case, I'll likely be asking Tsukasa and the others for their help.)

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Try to keep your show's runtime around an hour.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: You'll have a month to work on them. Then, we'll watch them and give you our assessments.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: ArcLand has told us not to pull any punches, so please try to understand.

rows.Speaker: Young Director Ａ
rows.Line: It's even scarier when he says that with a smile...

rows.Speaker: Young Director Ｂ
rows.Line: But we'll learn more by them picking us apart, so let's try to do our best.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“That's about it for the briefing.
We're looking forward to seeing your shows.”>

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Now then, we were going to call it there for the day...

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: But since we're all here, why don't we have ourselves a little test before you start working on your shows in earnest?

rows.Speaker: Young Director Ａ
rows.Line: A little test...?

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“There's no need for alarm, everyone.
Think of it as a piece of homework which will help you get to know your workshop peers better.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“The next time we meet, we'd like for you all to introduce yourselves through some short shows.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Introduce ourselves...?

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: You are directors, after all. Doesn't it make sense to let your direction do the talking?

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
The theme will be “rain”.
We're looking for shows around three minutes in runtime, to be performed in the arcade by the main entrance to ArcLand.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Of course, your shows will actually be performed here in this meeting room, so please keep that in mind.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
It'll be a one-man show.
We'd like to get an unbiased sense of your directing styles, so we've chosen an actor in advance to remove that particular variable.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: I'm sure you're all familiar with Asahi Genbu.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I see. Asahi can handle any role, so they'll immediately be able to see each director's capabilities.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It's the best way for them to size us up.)

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Please have scripts and directing plans ready by next time.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: Bring something good, okay?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Alright, this is the arcade where our shows will theoretically be staged.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Since it's so close to the entrance, guests of all ages should be present...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I'll want a show which fits in with the magical world of ArcLand, and also heightens anticipation and excitement for the wonderful time the guests are about to enjoy.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Still... I feel like I'm dreaming. Tom Gray himself will see this show...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(A show to introduce myself...
It's no simple task, but I need to do my best.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: To achieve that ArcLand feel, I'll want to include some elements of magic and fantasy.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Also, since this is my self-introduction, I'll need to tie in something which refers to me personally.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I know. I can revive some of the ideas I used for those surprise shows I did all those years ago...
One week later

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Argh! Why?!
It always rains on the days when I have something important planned!”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “The princess and I can't have our wedding in this weather!”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “Oh, you're completely soaked.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Would you like to rest at my house?
I have some hot soup.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (This is fascinating...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (With all of us working with the same theme, each director's style is clearly visible. I'm learning so much.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (And more importantly...)

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: That line at the end needs to carry a bit more implication.

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line: As it is now, things just end as a normal, day-to-day conversation. Try to be more conscious of impactful phrasing.

rows.Speaker: Young Director Ａ
rows.Line: I understand.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I appreciated the boldness of your story structure. Devices like that will help keep your audience's attention.”>

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line:
I agree.
Be careful not to rely overmuch on props, but...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Their feedback, born from their wealth of experience, covers every conceivable angle. Each and every remark from them is a pearl of directing wisdom.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (That alone makes my decision to participate in this workshop worth it.)

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: Next, we have Kamishiro. You're our last one.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Thank you.
Are you ready, Asahi?

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: I'm ready.

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “Hey, have you seen them before?”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “What am I talking about? The special flowers that bloom only during rainy days!”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “I came to look for them after hearing reports of sightings around here.”

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: The story of a botanist who wanders into the park in search of flowers that only bloom during rainy days.

rows.Speaker: Veteran Director
rows.Line: And through that search, he and the audience share special experiences you can only have when it rains, yes?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: That's correct.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“What a wholesome story.
It should appeal to children and grown adults alike.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Also, forgive me if I'm mistaken... But have you ever happened to watch 'The Voices of Honeybees'?”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “I have.”

rows.Speaker: Rui

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Geez, this place is covered in spiderwebs.
Creepy old mansion...”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Well, no matter.
I'll just clean it up, sell it and get it off my hands.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Hm...?
I thought I saw something cross the hallway just now.”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line:
“Who are you...?
None may set foot in this place without my permission...”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “Whoa!”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (This show is titled “Goodbye Ghosts”.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(Asahi is playing the protagonist, Luke.
A lonely young man who lost his family at a very young age.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (He's kind by nature, but has trouble forming relationships with others. As a result, he struggles to hold down work, and leads a bit of a desperate life.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But one day, Luke suddenly ends up inheriting an old mansion from a distant relative. That is where this story begins...)

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Okay, now I understand.
This distant relative of mine, due to being a real weirdo, decided to buy and live in a bona fide haunted mansion.”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line: “A weirdo? How rude... He was a good man, and a good housemate to us all.”

rows.Speaker: Actor B
rows.Line: “Yeah! All of us had a lot of fun together as friends♪”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “How many 'friends' are we talking about here?”

rows.Speaker: Actor C
rows.Line: “If you're talking about us ghosts, then I'd say around a hundred.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “There's no way that a hundred ghosts can fit inside this mansion! Wait, I'm not standing inside anyone right now, am I?!”

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Hehe...

rows.Speaker: Emu
rows.Line: This ghost story isn't very scary at all! It's actually really interesting!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes, and it includes many comical scenes. That means this show should appeal to everyone from children to grown adults.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (All of the ghosts living in this mansion are capricious and fickle. If they don't like the human residents, they'll use any and all means to run them out of the house.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Luke is strapped for cash, and needs to sell this mansion as quickly as possible. But he also knows that he won't earn very much in its current state.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (So, Luke begins to concoct a plan.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Ghosts linger in this world due to unresolved issues. If he can resolve the regrets of every ghost, they'll all vanish from the mansion.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Thus begins the monumental task of going around to every ghost, learning what anchors them to this world, and granting their last requests...)

rows.Speaker: Actor B
rows.Line: “What do I want to do?”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Tell me everything that comes to mind.
I'll do what I can to make it all happen.”

rows.Speaker: Actor B
rows.Line: “Hmm... There's so much...”

rows.Speaker: Actor B
rows.Line: “But I really wanna go somewhere with my mom and dad while holding their hands.”

rows.Speaker: Actor B
rows.Line:
“Because I was in the hospital for so long.
I wasn't really allowed to leave my bed...”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Wanting to see the people they cared about the most one last time. Wanting to apologize to friends who they parted from in anger.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Every ghost's wish is simple but heartfelt.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Some of them seem resentful and malicious at first, but underneath it all...)

rows.Speaker: Actor C
rows.Line:
“Thank you for helping me, Luke.
I feel much better now.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “All I did was bring your old lover to the mansion... Are you sure you're okay with how things went?”

rows.Speaker: Actor C
rows.Line: “I am. I got to scare him by pretending to be an evil spirit, so I'm sure he's over me now.”

rows.Speaker: Actor C
rows.Line:
“I mean, I really am like an evil spirit...
I felt so satisfied when I watched him crying day and night, unable to forget me.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “Does that really make you evil?”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “It's only natural to want someone precious to you to remember you after you've gone.”

rows.Speaker: Actor C
rows.Line:
“Yes, I know.
But I love him so much... I'll let him go.”

rows.Speaker: Nene
rows.Line: Wow...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Wow, indeed.
Asahi's rendition of Luke is remarkable, of course...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: But the ghosts' performances let you vividly picture their past lives, even when the details aren't shown on the stage.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (You can't see the ghosts' expressions due to the masks they're all wearing.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The masks represent the uncrossable line between the living and the departed. And by leaving the audience's minds to fill in their expressions, it makes it easier to empathize with the ghosts.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I understand the technique on an analytical level.)

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “It's just us left now, huh.”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line:
“Yes...
I'm amazed that you were able to help all the other ghosts.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Oh, is this wine my reward?
I did think it was an expensive vintage.”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line: “No, it was something I had stashed away before my death, and never got a chance to drink...”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line: “But now, I can say that I've fulfilled my wish of sharing it with a dear friend. That means I will vanish from this mansion tonight.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The more time lonely Luke spent with the ghosts, the more comfortable he became around them. He had found a place to call home.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (And so, each time he saw a friend off, the specter of that loneliness grew a little stronger.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (And this is the most important part of the story. The moment he says goodbye to the last one...)

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “Would you laugh if I told you that I feel sad right now?”

rows.Speaker: Actor A
rows.Line:
“No.
I believe that's the mark of a proper farewell.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“I see...
Yeah. You're right.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “When I was all by myself, I never actually felt lonely.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“But now, I'm all choked up...
My heart aches and I can't seem to stop crying.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line:
“Still, I'm glad we met...
I'm glad this haunted mansion came into my life.”

rows.Speaker: Asahi
rows.Line: “So, thank you.”

rows.Speaker: Sakaki
rows.Line:
I enjoy family-oriented stories quite a lot.
They seem simple, but many of them have deep depths too.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (As each ghost finds peace, the stage that was initially very lively grows emptier and emptier. A hole begins to grow in each audience member's heart.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But then comes the end... The narrow spotlight illuminating Luke's smile brings everything home.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (People come and people go. This story is the story of life itself.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (And even within the most final parting, there is still joy...a blessing. You feel that from the bottom of your heart.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (As a scriptwriter and director, he's miles ahead of me.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It doesn't matter how influenced I am by him, or how much I try to copy him.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The depth of the world he created, the weight of the message he's trying to send, everything...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I still have much to learn...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (How do I close that gap...?)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I have no idea. But...)
Rui's Room

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Before I begin work on the concept or script for my show, I should go over my objectives.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: First, I have to produce it from scratch.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: It must be completely original, and something that could be performed at ArcLand.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: And what I'll be aiming for is a show that appeals to all audiences. A show that has the power to bring everybody together.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Yes, just like “Goodbye Ghosts”.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I tried to achieve those objectives with my self-intro show...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: And I was told that it was “insipid”.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: The fact of the matter is that “Goodbye Ghosts” is miles ahead of anything I've ever made...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (It's difficult to put into words... But Tom's shows have “depth”.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The problem is, I have no idea how to capture that.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Digging deeper into the themes, adjusting the direction... All I can do right now is explore my options and see what sticks.

rows.Speaker: Math Teacher
rows.Line: Remember this formula, because you'll be using it a lot moving forward. And yes, it will be on the test.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (If I'm going to achieve that level of depth, then I'll need to find a theme I'm intimately familiar with.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Personally... Building machines, creating shows and school life immediately come to mind.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I could try different combinations of those things, and...

rows.Speaker: Math Teacher
rows.Line: Kamishiro, try solving problem three in the textbook for us.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: X-squared minus three.

rows.Speaker: Math Teacher
rows.Line: Correct.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I've come up with a number of ideas, but none of them seem to fit the bill.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(It works as a show...
But it also feels like it's been jury-rigged together using things taken from existing works.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (More to the point, I don't find it interesting.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I should start over.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I was hoping that a change of scenery would help me come up with better ideas...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (But my brain feels like it's at a standstill.)

rows.Line: I didn't mean to worry the others earlier.

rows.Line: (I should take a quick nap.)

rows.Line: (My body feels so heavy.)

rows.Line: (It's like something is tangled around my feet...)

rows.Line: Huh? Who said that just now?

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Oh, thank goodness. You're finally awake.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Luka...?

rows.Line: I'm sorry for waking you.

rows.Line: But you seemed to be suffering in your sleep.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(Ah, of course...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: If anything, I should thank you for waking me.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Still, Luka, what are you doing here?

rows.Line: Hehe. I was going to see if the plushies would like to take a nap on the stage with me.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: KAITO made so many fluffy cloud cushions for the show we're going to be doing soon.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: He said that I could use them within reason, so I was going to go invite everyone.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Doesn't it sound like you would have the most wonderful dreams?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I see. Yes, I'm inclined to agree with you.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: But your dream seemed more like a nightmare, Rui...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I'm not sure. I don't actually remember much of it.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
But it felt so real...
I didn't realize that it was a dream until I woke up just now.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: That sounds terrible...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(Still, that voice...
I remember hearing somewhere that dreams are manifestations of your innermost thoughts.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Perhaps I'm more deeply stressed than I had realized.)

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Oh, Rui, can I take this opportunity to toss you a little riddle?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: A riddle...?

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Yes. I'm sure you'll solve it right away.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: When someone is having a bad dream, but doesn't know that they're dreaming...

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: What's the best thing they can do to wake up?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Have someone else wake them up?

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Yes, that's right♪

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: That was the situation I was in just now, after all.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line:
Hehe. See?
You solved it right away.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: There are certain realizations that you can't make on your own. Things you can't see without someone else's help.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: So, if something is preventing you from having nice dreams...

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Then I think you should ask others for their help. To wake you up.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Isn't there someone perfectly placed to help you out with this problem?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Yes, I have more or less exhausted all of my options...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (If nothing I've tried has given me even a light at the end of the tunnel...)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Then I should try to solve this puzzle a different way.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: You're right. I can't stay stuck in this nightmare forever.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I don't know how well things are going to go, but I'll try what I can.

rows.Speaker: Luka
rows.Line: Good. I believe in you, Rui.

rows.Line: Okay, my headset and computer seem to be working well.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Now I just need to wait until it's time for us to meet.

rows.Speaker: Rui

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (I didn't expect them to agree to this so quickly. Honestly, I thought they were going to turn me away.)

rows.Line: (Not only that...)

rows.Line: “Thank you for taking the time out of your busy schedule to speak with me today.”

rows.Line: <“Not at all. I'm actually glad you came to ask for advice.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “I have to admit, I was surprised to hear that you had volunteered to be my advisor for this matter.”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I can't be there in person, but I still want to talk to as many of you as I can.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Also... Your self-intro show left a big impression on me.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I had a look over the concept document and script draft you sent me.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“It oozes with the desire to see your audience smile and have fun. But at the same time...”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I get the clear sense that you're trying desperately to overcome a great obstacle.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
“Yes.
This workshop has made it plainly obvious what I need to work on as a director.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “I asked to speak with you today to find a way to tackle those issues.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “It's actually something of a long story, but...”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“I see...
You want to produce shows with more depth.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “Yes. I had the chance to see the dress rehearsal for 'Goodbye Ghosts' the other day.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “I fully understand that comparing my work to your own is presumptuous in the extreme...”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “But at my current level, I cannot create shows that touch the heart like yours do. That fact is painfully clear to me now.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “After that, I broke down my script and directing plan to the best of my abilities, to see what else I could work into it.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “But the end result was simply a jury-rigged patchwork of ideas from other works.”

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “I believe that the problem lies with my approach to the assignment itself.”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Which is why you wanted a teacher to give you an objective diagnosis.”>

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: “Yes. I'm sorry for asking you to answer a question with such vague parameters...”

rows.Line: “But if you've noticed anything at all, I hope you'll tell me, frankly and candidly.”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“I see.”>

rows.Line: “As well as what effects and such will resonate with them the most...”

rows.Line: “I also consider the venue, and the demographics of the intended audience.”

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“I see.

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Which is a wonderful way to go about things...”>

rows.Line: <“But you may be taking it too far. I feel that you're subconsciously suppressing yourself.”>

rows.Line: “Until I encountered my current troupe, I performed my shows all alone.”

rows.Line: <“You weren't willing to bend because you wished to put on good shows, yes?”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“And in your mind, a 'good show' needs to make a large audience smile.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“In other words, as the director, you intentionally avoid putting in any more of your personal feelings than is necessary.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Because that is what allows you to make shows that resonate with the most people.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line:
<“Of course, that's not a bad thing.
If anything, that may be the most ideal stance a director could take.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“However, there are times when a show needs to be imbued with deeper feelings.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“It has to come from your own feelings and experiences. It can't be imagined or borrowed.”>

rows.Speaker: Tom
rows.Line: <“Obviously, you need to be careful not to take it too far. You wouldn't want to turn it into a monologue, after all. But...”>

rows.Line: <“Those raw feelings and experiences which are so powerful that even you hesitate to touch upon them... That's what gives a work depth. At least, that's what I believe.”>
